source.title: Two Speeds of Learning: A Representation-Readout Decomposition of Grokking and Double Descent
source.authors: Chi-Ning Chou; Oscar Uzdelewicz; Neng-Chun Chiu; Yao-Yuan Yang; SueYeon Chung

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: It tests grokking and its proposed learning dynamics using representation geometry, linear probes, and NTK alignment rather than the original sources’ task-specific circuit or Fourier progress measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports grokking accuracy curves for algorithmic tasks, representation and readout diagnostics, and a previously reported MNIST example with a standard-training comparison. Its discussion of other studies’ results is not recorded as study results. The figures contain additional plotted values that the text does not quantify.
record.test_reason: The study reproduces algorithmic grokking on six task-model pairs and a Liu et al. MNIST example. It tracks representation and readout diagnostics (critical dimension, linear probes, last-layer NTK alignment) through training and compares grokking with non-grokking counterparts. These are its own results bearing on V1, V2 and V3, plus an architecture comparison bearing indirectly on V6. The methods differ from the originals' Fourier/circuit progress measures.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that grokking reflects two speeds of learning: representation learning is gradual and active before onset, contrary to a strict lazy-to-rich account, while a faster readout stays train-biased until representations catch up. They argue MLPs and Transformers reach generalization via different geometric pathways. They diagnose the Liu et al. MNIST grokking, and label-noise double descent, as spurious effects of non-standard recipes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses grokking-style algorithmic tasks and train/test accuracy tracking, while adding a representation-readout decomposition with geometric, linear-probe, and NTK diagnostics. Task configurations and hyperparameters vary; the MNIST comparison changes initialization scale and training-set size together.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with task-model pair and seed: sparse-parity Transformer grokking occurs in only one of three seeds. The MNIST pattern is eliminated when initialization scale and training-set size are both changed to the reported standard condition.

fits_no_version.finding: Epoch-wise double descent on CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 with label noise shows representation degradation and noisy-label-dominated readout alignment. Both vanish without label noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-monotone generalization from label noise reflects representation deterioration followed by spurious-signal domination of readout gradients.

fits_no_version.finding: Train-test correlation of loss/accuracy changes turns negative with grokking. Representation metrics (NTK alignment, Ncrit, GLUE) keep correlation near 1 across β and tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation-geometry measures track generalization consistently across train and test even when accuracy curves diverge during grokking.

record.problems: The MNIST standard-training comparison changes initialization scale and training-set size together, preventing attribution to either factor alone. Several relevant accuracy and diagnostic values are shown only in figures; the reported cross-task representation-change ranges average over three seeds. No systematic within-task training-set-size sweep tests the delay-size relationship.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks. No within-task training-size sweep is reported; non-grokking counterparts change β and training size together.
Formation of a specific generalizing circuit (e.g. Fourier) and later removal of memorizing components; only task-agnostic geometry and readout measures are tracked.
Text or molecule data; weight norm as an independent switch; a clean initialization-scale-only manipulation on MNIST.
Entire version: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Entire version: no critical dataset size, ungrokking, or circuit-efficiency test. Weight-norm counterexamples are cited from others only.
Identification of the actual algorithm learned per run or architecture; only geometric pathways are compared.
Entire version: optimizer instabilities and softmax floating-point limits are not examined.

missing.what: Grokking switched on/off by output scale β with training size fixed: ModAdd Transformer, β=2 grokking vs β=0.3 non-grokking, both 60% train, 500 epochs
missing.locator: Appendix B.1.1 Table 1; Appendix D.2 Figures 22-27

missing.what: β sweep on ModAdd Transformer: train-test accuracy/loss correlation becomes negative for β>1, marking grokking onset
Architecture-dependent geometric mechanisms: MLPs increase ρc and decrease ρa, Transformers the opposite; R and D decrease in both
Pairwise Ncrit matrices and transfer probes: grokked models outperform non-grokked ones, with architecture-specific patterns

record.verdict_notes: r11 is not an experiment. The appendix is internally inconsistent about β: B.1 says large β pushes toward rich and produces grokking, while F.2 says large β induces lazy training. Non-grokking counterparts often change β, training size and epochs together, except the ModAdd Transformer. Most accuracy evidence is figure-only. V2 support rests on representation and readout measures, not circuit identification.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports grokking in algorithmic tasks, but does not systematically vary training-set size within a task to test whether smaller sets increase the delay.
It measures gradual representation change and train-biased readout alignment, but does not identify a Fourier/generalizing circuit or directly track removal of memorizing circuit components.

It studies an MNIST example and training-regime changes, but not text or molecules, and does not establish that genuine delayed generalization occurs broadly on non-algorithmic data. It does not test weight norm as an independent switch.
LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
The study does not test whether low norm favors a more efficient circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
It reports architecture-dependent geometric mechanisms, but does not identify and compare the algorithms learned across runs.
It does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point softmax limits as causes of grokking.

rows.subject: Six algorithmic task-model pairs
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of total critical-dimension decrease occurring in training phases before grokking onset.

conditions.value: modular addition, permutation composition, sparse parity

rows.measure: Fraction of total Ncrit drop before grokking onset.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as representation learning proceeding continuously before grokking onset, rather than beginning abruptly at onset.
rows.check: Besides V2, this row bears on the lazy-to-rich reading in V3. Ncrit falls before onset, which the authors present as contrary to a strict lazy-to-rich account. For V3 it shows the switch is not a lazy-then-rich transition. Test-side fractions can be as low as ~5% for some pairs, so pair-level strength varies.

source_check.correct: V2: observed gradual representation progress. V3: absent strict initially lazy phase; isolated initialization-scale switching cannot be determined from this measure.
source_check.problem: The shared observed state fits V2 but misstates the result against V3's strict lazy-to-rich interpretation.

rows.subject: Permutation composition MLP
rows.operation_detail: Tracked train-minus-test last-layer NTK-label alignment over training.
rows.baseline: Non-grokking counterparts have a substantially smaller gap.
rows.value: Large and positive throughout pre-grokking phases; peaks near training accuracy saturation and decays toward zero as grokking completes.
rows.note: The authors describe the gap as evidence of train-biased readout learning before grokking.

rows.subject: Algorithmic task-model pairs
rows.operation_detail: Compared mean train-minus-test NTK alignment across training phases.

conditions.value: modular addition, permutation composition, sparse parity

rows.measure: Mean NTK alignment difference, train minus test.
rows.baseline: Non-grokking counterpart maximum differences shown as controls.
rows.value: Typically largest in train100-to-onset, substantially exceeds pre-train100, and decays through onset-to-offset and post-offset; non-grokking gaps are substantially smaller.
rows.note: This measures readout alignment, not the formation or removal of identified circuit components.

rows.subject: MNIST MLP
rows.operation_detail: Used the previously reported high-initialization-scale, small-training-subset recipe; compared with a standard-training condition.
rows.measure: Delayed test generalization and final test accuracy.
rows.baseline: Standard condition: α = 1.0 and 10,000 train samples (16.7%); grokking pattern eliminated.
rows.value: Grokking pattern reported; final test accuracy around 80%.
rows.note: The authors diagnose the apparent delay as a readout artifact accompanied by degrading representations, not genuine representation improvement.
rows.check: The delayed generalization itself does appear on MNIST, so 'partial' understates the delay. The qualification is in the interpretation: authors attribute it to readout miscalibration over degrading representations, and final test accuracy is ~80%. That belongs in the label, not the state.

rows.subject: Support vector machine
rows.operation_detail: Compared MNIST test performance with the grokking MLP.
rows.note: This comparison indicates that the studied training recipe limits performance; it does not itself establish grokking.
rows.check: The SVM ~98% figure is a stated reference point, not a reported experiment of the study. It is not a measure of grokking and should not be a row, or at most context.

rows.subject: MNIST MLP
rows.operation_detail: Removed the high initialization scale and small-training-subset components of the grokking recipe.
rows.baseline: High-scale, small-subset recipe: α = 6.0 and 1,000 train samples; apparent grokking reported.
rows.value: The grokking pattern and diagnostic signatures were eliminated.
rows.note: Initialization scale and training-set size both change between conditions, so their individual effects cannot be separated.
rows.check: Relative to V3 (switching via initialization scale), the switch-off is observed, but α (6.0→1.0), training size (1k→10k) and epochs change together. The effect cannot be attributed to initialization scale alone.

source_check.correct: Recipe-level switch-off: observed, with grokking and diagnostic signatures eliminated. Effect attributable specifically to initialization scale: cannot_determine because scale, sample count and training duration change together.
source_check.problem: Confounded attribution is not a partially observed disappearance; the reported disappearance is complete.
